rule_text: Goods imported to be processed (finished, repacked, labelled, kitted) and then re-exported outside the UK, including to Ireland and the EU, can be placed under IPR. Goods sold on the UK market are not eligible.
Import duty and import VAT are suspended on goods that are processed and re-exported; duty only becomes payable if the goods are released to the UK market.
Suspension avoids paying duty up front: for goods re-exported within about 90 days the duty cash tied up (typically 2 to 3 months of duty) is not paid at all.
Running IPR costs about 18,000 GBP a year (systems, records, guarantee). It generally pays back once duty suspended on re-exported goods is above about 150,000 GBP a year.
High: authorisation takes 30 to 60 days, every movement needs stock and processing records, each authorisation must be discharged with export proof within 6 months, and quarterly returns are needed.

Approved by HMRC; guarantee of about 10 percent of suspended duty; records kept 4 years; goods identifiable throughout; exports must be supported by export declarations; no processing for UK-market sales.
HMRC audits discharge records. Missing export proof, late discharge or mixed UK and re-export stock lead to duty, interest and penalties, and can cost the authorisation.

Goods stored in an approved customs warehouse stay under duty and VAT suspension until released for free circulation. Suitable for slow-moving stock or goods that may be re-exported to Ireland or the EU.
Duty and import VAT are deferred until goods leave the warehouse for UK use and never paid on goods re-exported; no processing allowed beyond usual handling.
Cash benefit is the deferral of duty and VAT for the time stock is held, usually 45 to 120 days; strongest for stock held more than 60 days.
Worthwhile when about 200,000 GBP a year of duty is deferred or avoided on goods that sit in store or are re-exported; below that the warehouse running costs outweigh the benefit.
Medium: premises must be approved, an authorised warehousekeeper named, stock records updated within 24 hours of each movement and an annual physical stock take done.
Authorisation from HMRC; guarantee covering the duty and VAT at risk; records kept 4 years; goods stored no more than 3 years unless extended.
HMRC stock checks compare records to physical stock; shortages are charged duty and VAT plus penalties and repeated errors risk withdrawal of approval.
